payload.prompt: Create an invoice for the customer Windmill Ltd (org no. 994973150) with three product lines: System Development (6517) at 22950 NOK with 25% VAT, Maintenance (5339) at 8900 NOK with 15% VAT (food), and Consulting Hours (8246) at 10450 NOK with 0% VAT (exempt).

payload.goal: Create an invoice for Windmill Ltd with three product lines at different VAT rates: System Development at 25% VAT, Maintenance at 15% VAT, and Consulting Hours at 0% VAT.
success_checks: Customer Windmill Ltd with org no. 994973150 exists in the system
Product line 'System Development' (product no. 6517) is created/found with unit price 22950 NOK and 25% VAT
Product line 'Maintenance' (product no. 5339) is created/found with unit price 8900 NOK and 15% VAT
Product line 'Consulting Hours' (product no. 8246) is created/found with unit price 10450 NOK and 0% VAT
Invoice contains all three line items with correct VAT rates
Invoice is successfully created and assigned an invoice number
risk_notes: Sandbox is empty — customer Windmill Ltd must be created before invoice can be issued
All three products must be created or verified before being added to the order
Mixed VAT rates on a single invoice may require VAT account configuration per line
15% VAT (food/matmoms) must be explicitly mapped to the correct VAT code in Tripletex
0% VAT (exempt) must use the correct exemption code to avoid validation errors
No invoice date or due date provided — system defaults will be used; confirm if specific dates are required
No payment terms specified — risk of incorrect due date being applied
payload.suggested_first_action: Create customer Windmill Ltd via POST /customer with organizationNumber=994973150
ordered_steps: 1. POST /customer — create Windmill Ltd with organizationNumber=994973150
2. POST /product — create 'System Development' with productNumber=6517, price=22950, vatType=25%
3. POST /product — create 'Maintenance' with productNumber=5339, price=8900, vatType=15% (food/matmoms)
4. POST /product — create 'Consulting Hours' with productNumber=8246, price=10450, vatType=0% (exempt)
5. POST /order — create order linked to customer Windmill Ltd
6. POST /order/orderline — add line item: System Development (6517), qty=1, unitPrice=22950, vat=25%
7. POST /order/orderline — add line item: Maintenance (5339), qty=1, unitPrice=8900, vat=15%
8. POST /order/orderline — add line item: Consulting Hours (8246), qty=1, unitPrice=10450, vat=0%
9. PUT /order/{id}/invoice — convert order to invoice and confirm invoice number is assigned

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Update account.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.

Create new product.
Create order.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.

Send invoice by ID and sendType. Optionally override email recipient.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.
Add new department.
Create one employee.
Add new project.
Add activity.
Add project activity.
Create a project hourly rate.
Add new timesheet entry. Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination is supported.
Not found in spec

rules: For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Use query parameter sendType=EMAIL.
Method is PUT, not POST.
All params are QUERY PARAMETERS: paymentDate, paymentTypeId, paidAmount or paidAmountCurrency.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType.
Requires name and departmentNumber.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'STANDARD' unless admin is explicitly requested.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
If description text is provided, set description=<text>.
For fixed-price projects, set isFixedPrice=true and fixedPrice=<amount> (camelCase).
If name already exists (422 'Navnet er i bruk'), use GET /activity?name=... and reuse.
For project activities, set activityType='PROJECT_GENERAL_ACTIVITY'.
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.
For fixed rate: hourlyRateModel='TYPE_FIXED_HOURLY_RATE', fixedRate=<rate>.
Requires project, activity, employee, date, hours.
Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination.
hours is a decimal number (e.g. 8.0, 7.5).

1. Create an invoice for Windmill Ltd (org no. 994973150) with three product lines:

   - Maintenance (5339) at 8900 NOK with 15% VAT (vatType id 5)
   - Consulting Hours (8246) at 10450 NOK with 0% VAT (vatType id 6)

Following the playbook:
1. GET /ledger/account?number=1920 (bank setup)
2. PUT bank account to configure it


3. POST /customer for Windmill Ltd
4. Check if the products exist first since the sandbox pre-seeds them, then create any missing ones
5. POST /order, then batch create order lines, and finally POST /invoice

I'll start with the bank account and customer calls in parallel, then search for existing products before creating new ones.

I could make individual GET requests for each product number, but that's inefficient—let me see if I can batch these lookups or use a filter parameter to check multiple products at once.

I'll start by running the account lookup, customer creation, and all three product searches in parallel, then handle any missing products and proceed with the remaining operations like the bank setup, order creation, and invoice generation.

5. Create invoice

payload.headline: All 6 invoice checks failed despite successful API calls — likely wrong product IDs or VAT types
what_went_wrong: Products were fetched with GET /product (no filter) returning pre-seeded products, but the agent assumed IDs 84406477/78/79 matched product numbers 6517/5339/8246 — this mapping was never verified.
VAT type IDs (3, 5, 6) were hardcoded without lookup — if the sandbox uses different IDs for 25%/15%/0% VAT types, all orderlines would have wrong VAT, causing all checks to fail.

GET /product calls lacked productNumber filter params (e.g., ?number=6517), so the agent may have used wrong products entirely — the product IDs used may not correspond to the requested product numbers.
Score 0.0/8.0 with 0 errors suggests the invoice was created but with completely wrong data — wrong products, wrong VAT types, or wrong customer linkage.
what_worked: Bank account setup, customer creation, order creation, and invoice creation all succeeded with 0 HTTP errors.
Batch orderline creation via POST /order/orderline/list was efficient.
what_to_try_next: Use GET /product?number=6517 (and similarly for 5339, 8246) to correctly filter products by number instead of assuming positional IDs from unfiltered GET /product.
Look up VAT types via GET /ledger/vatType to get correct IDs for 25%, 15%, and 0% VAT before hardcoding them in orderlines.
Verify the product ID returned actually matches the requested product number before using it in orderlines — log and confirm the 'number' field in the response.
unnecessary_calls: GET /product (unfiltered, 3 times) — should use GET /product?number=6517 etc. to get correct product by number
GET /ledger/account (unfiltered) — could be more targeted with ?number=1920 filter to avoid ambiguity
